athena.deploy.completed.description: #4228 — the detached model deploy a land spawned has EXITED, with its code. Before this the only event was athena.trigger.started, so a deploy that refused was invisible and the land printed "merged + deployed + LIVE" over it (Wren's #4216). The land waits for this, or for athena.deploy.failed, before claiming the store carries the card's model changes.

deploy.allow_set_gate.passed.description: #3785 — the allow-set gate ran before an identity-touching deploy committed, and the store resolved a non-empty set of principals. Exists because on 2026-08-06 the doors came up reading an empty allow-set and the only signal was a warning on stderr that nobody was reading; the symptom surfaced minutes later as a human being told he was not on the team list. A warning is not a gate. Scoped to deploys whose diff touches identity surfaces, so it does not fire on docs cards and teach people to ignore it.

fields.detail: the gate's own line, including the principal count and the graph it resolved from

deploy.allow_set_gate.refused.description: #3785 — the allow-set gate REFUSED a deploy: the store resolved zero principals, or could not be asked at all. Both are refusals and the distinction is in the reason — could-not-ask is not the same as nobody-allowed, and neither is a safe deploy. Deploying either state would fail every door closed for everyone, including whoever would fix it. KNOWN GAP (#3788): non-zero is the wrong assertion. On 2026-08-07 the set held only three workers — non-empty, gate passed, and every human and agent was locked out of governed writes. The widened check asserts named presence, not a count.

fields.reason: why it refused — zero principals, or the store did not answer

test.completed.description: Werk test terminal phase: execution and best-effort model write-back have both returned. Verdict + counts + total duration are emitted on every run; execution_duration_ms and writeback_duration_ms expose the former hidden persistence tail.

fields.writeback_duration_ms: Wall-clock duration of TestSuiteRun and TestResult reflection

test.delta.description: Test run completed with delta vs prior run. #2193.

fields.count: How many registered needs-stack tests were not run
fields.saw: Per service, what the probe saw: http code and ms per try

fields.elapsed_secs: Wall-clock seconds for the whole run

test.scope.full.description: Werk `test` verb (#3821) — the loud escape to a FULL test run: an unmapped path or WERK_TEST_FULL. Never silent; carries the widening reason. The test-phase analogue of `build.scope.escaped`. Verb-substep event (#3513 naming law).

fields.units: Count of units in the full plan that will run

fields.changed: Count of changed files in the diff
fields.of: Total units available (scoped < of is the saving)
fields.scoped: Count of units the change scoped to

test.script.uncovered.description: Werk `test` verb (#3917) — a changed shell script that NO bats suite references. Named out loud so an unexercised script is a visible gap rather than dissolving into an empty selection (the blind spot #3917 fixed). Verb-substep event (#3513 naming law).

test.selection.description: Werk `test` verb (#3931) — the jest selection as EVIDENCE, not a count: which test files the runner picked and the reason each was chosen (related-file+registered), or the full-fallback reason in the same shape. Emitted so an under-selection is inspectable from the record alone — the log used to print only a count, and nobody could see whether the runner picked the RIGHT files. Verb-substep event (#3513 naming law).

fields.count: Number of selection rows (files, or 1 for a fallback row)
fields.files: Up to 8 selected file paths, semicolon-joined ('*' for fallback)
fields.reason: Why the first row was selected — uniform across rows today

A changed file in a unit that no test exercises is refused. Verb-substep event (#3513 naming law).

fields.tests: Number of registered test files the domains select
fields.untagged: Number of changed files no rule places

fields.level: error — the severity required by the Structured Logging Contract, derived from the event name
fields.message: Human-readable sentence: which case failed, in which file
fields.unit: Unit the case ran in (crate / package / suite)

testresult.lost.description: A run computed verdicts it could not store.
